patches.rationale: The current paginate uses zero-based indexing (start = page * page_size), so page=2, size=2 on range(1,8) returns items[4:6] == [5,6]. The issue requires one-based page numbers: page=2 must return [3,4]. Fix by computing start = (page - 1) * page_size. Preserve existing invalid-input guards (page < 1 or page_size < 1 -> []) and empty input behavior (slicing an empty sequence yields []). Pages beyond the last page naturally yield [] via slicing. Add a new regression test file covering the stated contracts.

from pagination import paginate


def test_issue_example_range_page2_size2():
    # Exact literal example from the issue: range(1, 8), page=2, size=2 -> [3, 4]
    result = paginate(range(1, 8), 2, 2)
    assert result == [3, 4]
    assert isinstance(result, list)


def test_page_numbers_are_one_based():
    # page=1 returns the first `size` items
    assert paginate(range(1, 8), 1, 2) == [1, 2]
    assert paginate(range(1, 8), 2, 2) == [3, 4]
    assert paginate(range(1, 8), 3, 2) == [5, 6]


def test_last_page_partial():
    # range(1, 8) has 7 items; page 4 size 2 -> [7]
    assert paginate(range(1, 8), 4, 2) == [7]


def test_page_beyond_last_page_returns_empty():
    assert paginate(range(1, 8), 5, 2) == []
    assert paginate(range(1, 8), 100, 2) == []


def test_empty_input_returns_empty():
    assert paginate([], 1, 2) == []
    assert paginate([], 2, 2) == []


def test_invalid_page_returns_empty():
    assert paginate([1, 2, 3], 0, 2) == []
    assert paginate([1, 2, 3], -1, 2) == []


def test_invalid_page_size_returns_empty():
    assert paginate([1, 2, 3], 1, 0) == []
    assert paginate([1, 2, 3], 1, -2) == []


def test_returns_list_type():
    assert isinstance(paginate([1, 2, 3], 1, 2), list)
    assert isinstance(paginate([], 1, 2), list)

patches.rationale: The paginate function already uses one-based indexing (start = (page-1)*page_size), but slicing a `range` object returns a `range`, not a `list`. The issue requires the exact example paginate(range(1,8), page=2, size=2) to return [3,4] (a list). The fix is to materialize the slice as a list. Empty/invalid inputs already return [] (a list), and beyond-last-page slices must also return [] as a list. I will wrap the slice in list(...) so all return paths yield lists, preserving the existing one-based semantics and invalid-input behavior. I will also add a new regression test file (distinct filename) covering the contracts with exact input expressions and result types.

from pagination import paginate


def test_issue_example_range_page2_size2_returns_list():
    # Exact literal example from the issue: range(1, 8), page=2, size=2 -> [3, 4]
    result = paginate(range(1, 8), 2, 2)
    assert result == [3, 4]
    assert isinstance(result, list)


def test_page_numbers_are_one_based():
    # page=1 returns the first `size` items
    assert paginate(range(1, 8), 1, 2) == [1, 2]
    assert paginate(range(1, 8), 2, 2) == [3, 4]
    assert paginate(range(1, 8), 3, 2) == [5, 6]


def test_last_page_partial_returns_list():
    # range(1, 8) has 7 items; page 4 size 2 -> [7]
    result = paginate(range(1, 8), 4, 2)
    assert result == [7]
    assert isinstance(result, list)


def test_page_beyond_last_page_returns_empty_list():
    result = paginate(range(1, 8), 5, 2)
    assert result == []
    assert isinstance(result, list)
    assert paginate(range(1, 8), 100, 2) == []


def test_empty_input_returns_empty_list():
    result = paginate([], 1, 2)
    assert result == []
    assert isinstance(result, list)
    assert paginate([], 2, 2) == []


def test_invalid_page_returns_empty_list():
    assert paginate([1, 2, 3], 0, 2) == []
    assert paginate([1, 2, 3], -1, 2) == []


def test_invalid_page_size_returns_empty_list():
    assert paginate([1, 2, 3], 1, 0) == []
    assert paginate([1, 2, 3], 1, -2) == []


def test_list_input_returns_list():
    result = paginate([1, 2, 3, 4], 2, 2)
    assert result == [3, 4]
    assert isinstance(result, list)
